newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures ended higher but off their highs on Friday while the franc and September PIBOR futures weakened at the end of the day as investors took defensive positions ahead of a meeting of EU finance ministers on Sunday and Monday.

Dealers said the mark was in demand against the franc, lira and peseta because of concern and uncertainty about what position the new Socialist-led government of France will take on European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
June PIBOR finished unchanged after trading in a four basis point range all day.
"The Ecofin on Monday is going to be quite critical for all of us," said a bond analyst in Paris. "It will give us the first signal of what road the (French) socialists are going to take."
The franc weakened to touch a low of 3.3763 per mark compared to 3.3718 early in the session. AT 1500 GMT, the franc was trading at 3.3758 per mark.

"There's good demand for the mark against all European currencies, especially against the lira and the peseta more than the franc, on worries ahead of the weekend because of doubts...about the possibility of a delay to EMU," a trader said. He added that sterling weakness helped the mark climb.
French markets failed to react durably to U.S. May payrolls, which, combined with upwardly revised April and March reports, showed the U.S. labour market was strong and tightening.
U.S. analysts said the report increased the chances of an interest rate increase later this year in the United States.
The OAT/Bund spread narrowed to minus six basis point from minus nine.
The dollar weakened suddenly in the afternoon, sparking talk that European central banks had sold the dollar when it rose above 1.74 marks.
